source.title: The Implicit Regularization of Dynamical Stability in Stochastic Gradient Descent

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; some mathematical symbols and figure content are flattened, but the relevant prose and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and numerically evaluates a different account of generalization based on dynamical stability and sharpness, measuring test error alongside training behavior for SGD and GD in two simple model families. It conceptually tests optimizer and measured-property versions, but not the named benchmark versions or their specific recipes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own numerical comparisons of SGD and GD as learning rate varies, plus its reported sharpness and path-norm measurements. Theoretical claims and cited results are not separate result rows. Values visible only in figures are recorded as figure only; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study investigates stability, learning rate, and generalization in synthetic regression models, but its results test none of V1–V8. SGD versus GD does not test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison. Its Fisher-matrix sharpness measures do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or ranking of generalization gaps. The SGD–GD comparison also lacks V5's fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors derive stability-based sharpness and parameter-norm controls and generalization bounds for two-layer ReLU and diagonal linear networks. Both SGD and GD have generalization guarantees in the ReLU analysis; the stronger distinction favoring SGD is established for diagonal linear networks. Numerical results support benefits of larger learning rates, while some observed ReLU advantages of SGD remain unexplained by their stability bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies stability-induced regularization in synthetic two-layer ReLU and diagonal linear models with large initialization, gradient clipping, and learning-rate sweeps; it does not reproduce the benchmark settings in the claim versions. Theoretical analysis is accompanied by numerical validation.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and optimizer affect reported test error and sharpness measurements; for the diagonal linear network, SGD's test error decreases significantly with learning rate while GD's barely changes.

fits_no_version.finding: In two-layer ReLU regression, increasing learning rate improves both optimizers' test performance; SGD remains better with the authors' adjusted learning-rate comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can generalize better than GD in synthetic two-layer ReLU regression even with learning rates adjusted for their theoretical bounds.

fits_no_version.finding: ReLU-network Fisher trace and path norm decrease with increasing SGD learning rate; GD spectral sharpness approaches its stability bound at sufficiently large learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate constrains distinct Fisher sharpness measures for SGD and GD in the tested ReLU model.

fits_no_version.finding: In diagonal linear regression, increasing SGD learning rate substantially lowers test error and Fisher trace, while spectral sharpness changes little; GD test error and sharpness measures barely change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested diagonal linear model, Fisher trace captures learning-rate-dependent generalization changes that spectral sharpness does not.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD reaches approximately balanced diagonal linear factorizations across the tested initial imbalances, whereas GD preserves imbalance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD promotes balanced factorization more strongly than GD in the tested diagonal linear model.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: Numerical results are presented in figures without exact values in the text; the experiments use simple synthetic models and data rather than image or language benchmarks. The text says large initialization and gradient clipping are used, with clipping inactive near convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct numerical result rows were left out. Theoretical bounds, statements about clipping activation in Figure 1, and cited prior-work results are not treated as independent result rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, limited versus broader tuning, and the specified remedies and benchmark exceptions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to the training recipe that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdict: absence of an adaptive-optimizer experiment is untested scope, not evidence qualifying V4. All corrected row states indicate inability to determine a listed version, rather than unreadable qualitative findings.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label versus natural-label comparison, and no Inception, AlexNet, or MLP memorization-capacity test.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold or test-error-versus-width result.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

Tests SGD versus GD on two-layer ReLU and diagonal linear networks as learning rate changes; does not compare adaptive optimizers such as Adam, benchmark tuning breadth, language models, or weight-decay and optimizer-switching remedies.
No batch-size sweep or large-batch training comparison.

Measures Fisher-matrix sharpness and path norm as learning rate varies, alongside test error; does not test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compare its ranking with norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal or retraining comparison.
